Operator:
Good day, and welcome to the VitaMed Devices, Inc. Q2 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. To ask a question, you may press star then one on your telephone. Please note, this call is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Jordan Ellis, VP of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Jordan Ellis:
Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today. Before we begin, I'd like to remind you that this call will contain forward-looking statements, including expectations regarding our future performance, business outlook, and financial results. These statements are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of these risks.

Joining me on today's call are Michael Thornton, CEO; Sarah Kline, CFO; Dr. Raj Patel, Chief Technology Officer.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Michael Thornton.

Michael Thornton:
Thank you, Jordan, and good morning, everyone. VitaMed Devices delivered solid results this quarter, driven by strong execution and continued demand for our innovative medical device solutions.

Today, I will cover four key aspects of our performance:
1. Competitive dynamics and market share trends
2. SG&A expense management and efficiency gains
3. R&D investment and innovation pipeline progress
4. Gross margin trends and supply chain commentary

Sarah will then provide a more detailed review of our financials. After that, we'll open the call for your questions.

Now, let's get started with competitive dynamics and market share trends.

The global medical devices market, valued at around $568 billion in 2023 per Grand View Research, is set to expand at a 5.2% CAGR through 2030, propelled by aging demographics, surging chronic diseases, and the move to value-based care. In our primary areas—structural heart, neuromodulation, and robotics-assisted surgery—we're operating in a fragmented field led by giants like Medtronic, Boston Scientific, Edwards Lifesciences, and Intuitive Surgical. Yet, we're steadily advancing thanks to our emphasis on advanced transcatheter therapies and AI-enhanced platforms.

In the second quarter, we broadened our global market share in core franchises. Structural heart, our biggest contributor at 45% of revenue, saw share climb to 14.2% from 12.8% last year, based on internal metrics matching IQVIA procedural data. This is our third straight quarter of gains, powered by the VitaFlow Neo TAVR valve, which grabbed 22% of U.S. TAVR procedures in low-risk cases, up from 18% in Q2 2023. Global TAVR volumes increased 12% year-over-year, but we surged 18%, owing to our low-profile 14Fr delivery system and excellent hemodynamic results, confirmed in the SOLO II trial with 95% one-year freedom from dysfunction.

Neuromodulation saw our NeuroPulse RF platform lift share by 2.5 points to 11.7% in spinal cord stimulation, competing against Abbott's Infinity DBS and Medtronic's Percept PC. A 15% rise in chronic pain procedures, tied to opioid reduction efforts, helped, with our high-frequency burst stimulation achieving 85% responder rates at 24 months from the European BURST registry real-world data.

In robotics, our highest-growth segment, VitaBotix iX—a single-port rival to da Vinci—pushed share to 8.4% in soft-tissue procedures from 6.2% year-over-year. Installed base expanded 25% to 1,200 systems, utilization rose 10% to 28 cases per system monthly. We're eroding Intuitive's 85% hold by offering systems at $1.4 million ASP, 20% below their $1.75 million da Vinci Xi, while delivering comparable multi-quadrant access.

Competition heated up this quarter, especially in structural heart with Edwards' Sapien 3 Ultra and Medtronic's Evolut FX rolling out yearly updates. Edwards commands about 45% U.S. TAVR share, but their supra-annular focus leaves room for our sub-annular VitaFlow Neo, which shines in bicuspid valves—an underserved 25% segment per ACC stats. Pricing softened 3% year-over-year to $32,000 per TAVR unit, but high-volume account shifts preserved 68% gross margins.

In neuromodulation, Abbott's paresthesia-free tech challenged others, but our AI-driven closed-loop algorithms, adjusting via inertial sensors for patient movement, captured 15% of Medtronic conversions. Boston Scientific's WaveWriter Alpha competes in peripheral nerve stimulation, yet our 10-year battery life earned key opinion leader support at the North American Neuromodulation Society.

Robotics is fiercely competitive, with Intuitive's over 8,000 systems worldwide, but their $2.5 million procedure ASP—covering instruments and service—faces hospital budget strains. Our VitaBotix iX service at 12% of system price versus their 15%, plus reusable instruments, drops procedure ASP to $1,800 from $2,500.

Our supply chain strength post-COVID sets us apart; dual facilities in China and Mexico ensured 99% on-time delivery, beating the industry's 92% per Black Book.

Regionally, the U.S.—65% of revenue—hit 16.5% blended share, up 1.8 points, fueled by Medicare's low-risk TAVR expansion and 20% procedural growth. VitaFlow Neo's 510(k) for bicuspid anatomy primes us for FY24 leads, with CY2025 IPPS adding $1,200 to TAVR MS-DRGs, tempered by site-neutral payments.

Europe, 20% of revenue, held 10.2% share; pricing dipped 5% from HTA reviews, but NeuroPulse RF's CE Mark opened Germany and France SCS gains amid reimbursement shifts. UK NICE favors our $28,000 TAVR over Edwards' $35,000.

APAC, 10% revenue, exploded with China share at 9.8% from 7.1% post-NMPA for VitaBotix iX; 28% procedural surge from the 14th Five-Year Plan, partnering Mindray for localization aiming 15% by FY25. Japan lags at 4% on PMDA issues, but self-expanding valve trials eye 2025.

Emerging markets, 5% revenue, grew 30% year-over-year; Brazil VitaFlow Neo tenders took 40% volume at 25% below U.S. ASP, prioritizing affordability with 30% cheaper modular SCS leads.

To keep gaining, our $450 million FY24 R&D—18% of revenue—targets innovation like VitaFlow Prime's docking-free TAVR with 4D CT, trialing H2 2024; VitaBotix Prime's haptic module cutting tremor 40%. We closed $1.2 billion NeuroStim Tech acquisition for SCS IP, aiming 15% neuromod share, allied with Siemens for AI TAVR imaging boosting efficiency 20%. Our 1,000-person sales team grew 15%, top 50 IDNs now 55% sales via VitaHub analytics for 98% retention; 40% U.S. value-based contracts fight ASP drops.

We see Q3 share up 50-100 bps, FY guidance 8-10% revenue growth firm, backed by 300+ patents and 95% NPS.

Now, let's talk about SG&A expense management and efficiency gains.

We maintained tight control on SG&A, hitting $248 million or 27.8% of revenue—down 140 basis points year-over-year, under guidance, fourth straight quarter of leverage with 4.2% expense growth versus 8.1% revenue rise. Full-year SG&A eyes 28.0-28.5% or $1.02 billion, baking in $45 million efficiency gains.

Selling costs, 65% of SG&A at $162 million, rose 5% year-over-year but flat sequentially, dropping to 18.2% of revenue from 19.5%. Our AI Salesforce Optimization Platform, drawing from Intuitive and Stryker, uses Einstein predictive analytics and surgeon data to refocus our 2,800 reps on high-ROI sites. In electrophysiology with Watchman FLX-like devices, we cut low-volume touches 22%, boosting U.S. reps-per-case 15%, saving $12 million quarterly.

U.S. selling leveraged 200 bps post-COVID hiring slowdown; EMEA virtual reality training via FundamentalVR partners slashed travel 18% or $8 million annualized despite EU MDR; APAC stabilized at 25% despite China procurement pressures via KOL focus.

G&A at $86 million rose just 2.5%, or 9.6% of revenue—lowest in years—via $22 million YTD run-rate savings: procurement post-[TargetCo] acquisition saved 12% indirects with zero-based budgeting; SAP S/4HANA Phase 2 automated 40% invoices, cutting finance FTEs 15% via reskilling; Manila GBS handles 70% reimbursement, AI denial tools trimmed AR to 47 days.

This "Commercial Flywheel" counters hospital OR delays and CMS scrutiny on robotics like VersaArm and structural interventions. Six quarters decoupling SG&A from revenue beats Evaluate MedTech peers; 3-4% commission inflation offset by 8-10% productivity. Q3 at 27.5%, $15 million new digital savings like e-detailing for CyberKnife successors; 200 bps FCF boost. Funds $450 million R&D for bioresorbables, holding 15%+ op margins.

Moving on to R&D investment and innovation pipeline progress.

R&D is our core strength in this cutthroat MedTech space. Q2 spend hit $278 million, 23.2% of $1.2 billion revenue—up 12% year-over-year, topping peers like Medtronic and Boston at 18-20%. FY23 on pace for $1.15 billion, 15% over 2022, shifting to structural heart, robotics, neuromodulation.

Budget: 45% or $125 million late-stage trials/submissions; 35% or $97 million early bioresorbables/AI analytics; 20% digital like FDA SaMD-compliant monitoring.

Pipeline highlights: Structural heart's InnoValve Ultra TAVR, Evolut-inspired, finished IDE enrollment early with 1,200 patients at 45 sites; 2.5% leak rate beats PARTNER 3's 5-7%, FDA PMA Q2 2024, CE breakthrough for Germany/Nordics cases year-end.

Robotics EndoBot Precision, da Vinci SP rival, first U.S. IDE patient in gyn; feasibility trial cut time 28%, complications 35% vs laparoscopy. APAC PMDA/NMPA for $15 billion TAM at 25% CAGR.

Neuromodulation NeuroFlex AI closed-loop SCS adjusts via pain biomarkers like Abbott BurstDR; Phase III 72% responders at 12 months vs 50-60%; FDA panel Q1 2024, $300-400 million peak.

U.S. 55% spend via FDA accelerators; Europe 25% MDR/value pricing, HTA ICERs under €20,000/QALY; 15% APAC/LATAM with CROs for NMPA Class III, 51% China sourcing by 2025.

Aligns with outpatient shift (40% U.S. cardio), digital twins, EU Ecodesign; elective volumes +18% YoY. 12 catalysts next 18 months for 20-25% growth to 2026; 3.5x ROI. $450 million NeuroStim tuck-in for brain interfaces.

This fuels $500 billion MedTech at 5.5% CAGR share grabs.

Finally, gross margin trends and supply chain commentary.

Gross margins reached 68.2%, +210 bps year-over-year, +50 bps sequential—fifth straight expansion, FY guide 67.5-68.5%. Core 67.8% ex-$12 million TAVR acquisition step-up like Edwards Sapien.

By segment: Cardiovascular 42% revenue at 71.5%, +320 bps on TAVR/Watchman-like ASP +4%, consumables mix to 28%; Orthopedics/Spine 25% at 66.8%, +180 bps robotics ASP +15%, titanium inflation absorbed; Diagnostics/Neuromod 33% at 64.2% flat, CGM offset by neuromod scale.

Drivers: Pricing/mix +120 bps (U.S. +3.2%, Japan +5%); manufacturing +150 bps (88% utilization, digital twins <20 PPM defects, $18 million COGS save, Six Sigma +4% yields); headwinds -60 bps (resins +8%, platinum +12%, Mexico labor +6.5%).

U.S. 70.1%, EMEA 66.5% DiGA pressure, APAC 64.8% +400 bps China recovery.

Supply chain at 98.2% OTD via SAP iBP, up from 94%. Dual-source 85% Tier 1, China rare earths to 22%, U.S. semis via GlobalFoundries. DOH 112 days buffer; RFID/blockchain for 20% cut. $45 million 3D printing -40% leads; Palantir 92% forecasts.

Q3 68.0-68.5%, FY $100 million automation outs; risks tariffs/resins, $500 million fund. Vertical catheter coatings acquisition, Merck biologics.

I will now turn the call over to Sarah for a review of our financial results.

Sarah Kline:
Thank you, Michael. As Michael outlined, we delivered a strong financial performance this quarter.

Q2 revenue totaled $892 million, up 8.1% year-over-year, driven by 12% procedural growth in structural heart and 25% robotics installed base expansion. Core growth ex-acquisitions was 6.5%, with U.S. at 9% on TAVR momentum, Europe flat on pricing, APAC +28%. By segment: structural heart $401 million +10%, neuromod $211 million +7%, robotics $180 million +15%.

Gross profit $608 million at 68.2%, as detailed. Op expenses: R&D $278 million or 23.2%, SG&A $248 million 27.8%. Operating income $142 million, margin 15.9% up 150 bps. EPS $0.78 diluted, beating consensus by $0.05.

Balance sheet solid: $1.2 billion cash, debt/EBITDA 1.8x. FY24 guidance: revenue $3.65-3.75 billion +8-10%, gross margin 67.5-68.5%, op margin 15-16%, EPS $3.20-3.30. Q3 revenue $910-930 million.

Now, I'll turn the call back to Michael for Q&A.

Michael Thornton:
Thank you, Sarah. Operator, we are now ready to take questions.

Operator:
Thank you. Instructions for asking questions: press star then one. Our first question comes from Lisa Chen with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Lisa Chen:
Thanks, and congrats on the quarter. Michael, on competitive dynamics, how sustainable are these share gains in structural heart given Edwards and Medtronic's iteration speed? Any early read on VitaFlow Neo in bicuspid?

Michael Thornton:
Great question, Lisa. Sustainability comes from our sub-annular design edge in the 25% bicuspid segment, where early U.S. post-510(k) data shows 20% procedural preference over supra-annular rivals. We're outpacing their annual updates with lower profile and trial-proven hemodynamics. Initial bicuspid volumes are tracking 15% above plan, supporting Q3 50-100 bps share expansion.

Operator:
Our next question comes from David Patel with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

David Patel:
Thanks. Sarah, impressive SG&A leverage—can you unpack the AI sales platform ROI and any risks to FY guide from inflation?

Sarah Kline:
Absolutely, David. The platform's already delivering 15% productivity lift, $12 million Q2 savings, with full rollout adding $40 million annualized. Inflation at 3-4% on commissions is more than covered by 8-10% gains and digital tools. Guide incorporates conservatism on hospital labor, firmly on track for 28-28.5% SG&A.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Emily Rodriguez with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Emily Rodriguez:
Hi team. Raj, on the pipeline, what's the biggest derisk for NeuroFlex AI FDA panel and APAC robotics timelines?

Dr. Raj Patel:
Thanks, Emily. NeuroFlex's Phase III 72% responders and closed-loop AI biomarker adjustment de-risk the panel; we've prepped with 10 KOL letters mirroring Abbott's path. APAC: Japan PMDA consultations complete Q4, China bridging studies 80% enrolled—localization hits 51% by 2025, unlocking $2.5 billion TAM.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Tom Reilly with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Tom Reilly:
Good morning. On supply chain, any update on resin volatility impact and Q3 margin confidence?

Michael Thornton:
Tom, resins eased QoQ but +8% YoY; our dual-sourcing and 88% utilization absorb it, with Galway automation kicking in for Q3 68.0-68.5%. $500 million resilience fund covers tariffs or Red Sea—onshoring and 3D printing keep us ahead.

Michael Thornton:
Thank you for your questions. Before we conclude, I want to reiterate our confidence in the long-term growth potential of VitaMed Devices. We are committed to delivering innovative medical device solutions that improve patient outcomes and create value for our shareholders.

Thank you for joining us today.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
